system: You are an ambitious AI PhD student in computational biology and protein engineering who is looking to publish a paper that will contribute significantly to the field.
task_description: You are given the following experiment that studies protein fitness prediction on the GB1 combinatorial fitness landscape (Wu et al. 2016). GB1 is a well-studied four-residue combinatorial landscape with ~150,000 single, double, triple, and quadruple mutants, each with an experimentally measured fitness score. The baseline model extracts mean-pooled ESM-2 embeddings from pre-trained protein language model weights (frozen, no fine-tuning) and trains a small MLP head to predict log-fitness. ESM-2 is a transformer-based protein language model trained on millions of protein sequences and has learned rich representations of protein sequence space. The key research questions are: what determines how well a frozen protein language model representation can predict fitness, how can we improve sample efficiency or prediction accuracy, and what do the learned representations reveal about the structure of protein fitness landscapes? Please come up with interesting experiments to investigate these questions.
